lines: Behind the Classes door, the Class Library now lists every class.
It opens with Classes, and the promise: ride a video alone, or join a group. The bike follows either way.
Three shelves, by length: twenty minutes, thirty, and sixty for endurance, each with its tagline.
Each open card shows its cover, its length, a resistance profile drawn from its plan, its title, its channel and focus.
An open card leads to that class's Class Start.
The Class length tabs show one shelf, or all of them. The arrow keys move between tabs, from the keyboard too.
A new rider starts at level one. A class above that is locked, and says the level that opens it.
A locked card stays in the tab order, so a screen reader announces the level, and it leads nowhere.
With no catalogue to read and none kept on the device, the library says so, and Try again asks again.
The same library, from one column on a phone to three on a desktop.
What the tests prove: five behaviour specs through the page, all green, and the first bundle still under budget.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
